facts.value: Educational psychology is the study of how humans learn in educational settings, the effectiveness of educational interventions, the psychology of teaching, and the social psychology of schools as organizations.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Educational psychologists can be found in preschools, schools of all levels, including post-secondary institutions, community organizations and learning centers, Government or private research firms, and independent or private consultants.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The work of developmental psychologists such as Lev Vygotsky, Jean Piaget, and Jerome Bruner has been influential in creating teaching methods and educational practices.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Educational psychology is often included in teacher education programs in North America, Australia, and New Zealand.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: School psychology combines principles from educational psychology and clinical psychology to understand and treat students with learning disabilities; to foster the intellectual growth of gifted students; to facilitate prosocial behaviors in adolescents; and otherwise to promote safe, supportive, and effective learning environments.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: School psychologists are trained in educational and behavioral assessment, intervention, prevention, and consultation, and many have extensive training in research.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
